title: Man. Post. Cap. X tip — we are punished for Adam’s sin via propagated corruption, not immediately
pass_a_gloss: In Adam’s posterity God saw all the malice of Adam’s disobedience—hereditary corruption: unbelief, habitual enmity toward God, clash with nature’s law, etc.—and likewise sentenced like evils with like penalties. Nature’s law demands that like evils fare alike. So we are punished for Adam’s sin, but through propagated corruption; those penalties are not immediate.
pass_b_english: In Adam’s posterity God saw all the malice of Adam’s disobedience, hereditary corruption—that is, unbelief, habitual enmity against God, opposition to the law of nature, and the like—and likewise sentenced like evils to like penalties.
For the law of nature demands that it go equally ill with equal evils.
We are therefore punished on account of Adam’s sin, but through the mediation of propagated corruption; those penalties are not immediate.
source_text: Vidit in posteris Adami Deus malitiam omnem inobedientiae Adami, corruptionem haereditariam, hoc est, incredulitatem, inimicitiam habitualem adversus Deum, legi naturae repugnantiam &c., similiter malis similibus poenis addixit. Flagitat enim naturae lex, ut pariter malis, pariter male sit. Punimur ergo propter peccatum Adami, sed mediante corruptione propagata, non immediate sunt illae poenae.

choices.choice: Punished via propagated corruption, not immediate
